subject: Privacy ledger sampling plan & DPIA evidence follow-up
messages:
From: Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@brightwellhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Brightwell Health Legal <legal@brightwellhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 08:12:00 -0000
Subject: Request: privacy ledger sampling + DPIA evidence (Art. 28/30)

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of Brightwell's DPIA and ongoing data-transfer due diligence, our privacy team needs a small sampling of the processing ledger (Art. 30 extract) and a short plan describing how Redwood will provide evidence for subprocessors and cross-border transfers during our audit window.

Specifically we need:
- A CSV export with a sample of processing activities (schema: activity_id, data_types, purpose, legal_basis, recipient_country, subprocessors) — ~50 rows is fine.
- A short playbook (1–2 pages) describing how you will surface DPIA-relevant evidence (logs, KMS attestations, onshore hosting options) if we request it during the audit window.
- Confirmation of audit rights scope (can Brightwell request a focused remote review for processors/controls related to our account?).

Could you confirm whether Redwood can provide the above by EOD Wed 17 Mar? If you need a narrower scope to start, indicate that and we can prioritize.

Also looping in legal for any formalities.

Best,
Amelia Torres
Privacy Officer
Brightwell Health

[Attachment: DPIA-request-template.docx (referenced)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@brightwellhealth.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request: privacy ledger sampling + DPIA evidence (Art. 28/30)

Hi Amelia — thanks for the clear ask and for looping in legal. We can support this; below is a proposed plan and timeline.

Summary plan (high level):
1) Provide a 50-row sampled ledger CSV that redacts any PII by default but preserves schema and recipient_country for transfer mapping. (Attached: privacy-ledger-sample.csv)
2) Deliver a 1–2 page DPIA evidence playbook that describes what artifacts we can produce on short notice: Art. 28 subprocessor inventory, Article 30 processing ledger export, KMS key rotation logs, retention policy excerpts, and onshore hosting options. (Attached: dpia-support-checklist.pdf)
3) Confirm audit rights: Redwood supports focused remote evidence reviews scoped to account-relevant subprocessors and systems; for on-site or deep-dive access we will coordinate an operational plan with your legal team.

Timeline:
- Today (14 Mar): share sample CSV + playbook draft (attached).
- Tue 16 Mar: internal QA pass and incorporation of any Brightwell comments.
- Wed 17 Mar EOD: finalize artifacts and provide delivery link / secure share.

Next actions for Redwood team: Hannah, can you validate that the sample CSV redaction process removes user identifiers but leaves necessary mapping columns? Jonas, can you confirm the export includes recipient_country values for transfer mapping? Marissa, please prepare a short note on audit logistics and whether we require an NDA for privileged exchanges.

Amelia — if that timeline works we will proceed. If Brightwell needs the raw ledger with less redaction, let us know and we will route through legal for a data-sharing agreement.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: privacy-ledger-sample.csv (CSV) — sample rows included]
[Attachment: dpia-support-checklist.pdf (PDF)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@brightwellhealth.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:22:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request: privacy ledger sampling + DPIA evidence (Art. 28/30)

Thanks, Soojin — quick technical clarifications for Brightwell so the sample meets your DPIA needs.

- The ledger extract we attach includes an activity_id, purpose, legal_basis, recipient_country, and subprocessors columns. We will pseudonymize user identifiers (user_hash) by default; if you need reversible mapping we require a legal basis + Data Processing Addendum (DPA) amendment.
- For cross-border mapping, recipient_country is derived from our subprocessor region tags; if you need exact datacenter locations we can provide on a limited basis under an amendment.
- Art. 30 register: we can provide the extract in CSV and JSON. The CSV attached here shows the format. If you need additional fields (e.g., retention_period_days), please flag.

Related internal note: our secure share will be a time-limited link from the compliance vault (see link below). We will also retain a snapshot for audit purposes and can produce a redacted transcript of access logs if required.

Internal link: https://app.redwood.com/records/HS-9823

On the audit rights question: we support remote evidence requests scoped to relevant processors and controls. For anything beyond remote reviews (e.g., vendor-supplied logs exposing privileged system telemetry) we will request a mutually agreed scope and an NDA if Brightwell requires it.

Jonas Weber
Director, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference

> On Sun, Mar 14, 2027 at 08:12 AM Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@brightwellhealth.com> wrote:
> > Thanks for taking this on. As part of Brightwell's DPIA and ongoing data-transfer due diligence...

From: Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@brightwellhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Brightwell Health Legal <legal@brightwellhealth.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 16:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request: privacy ledger sampling + DPIA evidence (Art. 28/30)

Hi all,

Thanks — that timeline and the sample look good. A couple quick notes from legal: we will accept the pseudonymized CSV for now; please include the retention_period_days column if easy. For recipient_country, the region tag is sufficient.

We do want the audit to be documented in our audit plan with Redwood as a processor-level remote review. I will send a short statement of scope and a simple amendment for the DPA, primarily to allow reversible mappings if later needed. Expect that from legal by end of day Tuesday.

Two asks:
1) Can Redwood confirm whether any subprocessors used for logging/observability are located outside the EU/US? A short list in the playbook will suffice.
2) Please provide the secure share link for the sample CSV and playbook when ready.

If those are OK we'll schedule a 30-minute sync on Wed to walk through artifacts.

Thanks,
Amelia Torres
Privacy Officer
Brightwell Health
